deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's preparatory notes for the Nov–Dec 1966 IHES talks on crystals and de Rham cohomology. On the previous page he computed H^1_dR of the formal affine line over W = W(k) (Witt vectors of the perfect residue field k, uniformizer p) using the Tate algebra W{t} of restricted power series. He found that this H^1 is not finitely generated, even modulo torsion; he notes it has infinite rank over W. The reason is that Σ a_n t^n is the derivative of a restricted series iff |a_n|_p/|n+1|_p → 0. Because v_p(n+1) is unbounded, a_n → 0 is not enough.

This page comments that this divisibility condition on the coefficients is 'biscornue' (awkward). He then describes the Monsky–Washnitzer remedy, which replaces it with a stronger and more natural condition: overconvergence. A series is overconvergent if there is some ρ > 1, depending on the series, with |a_n| = O(ρ^{-n}). Equivalently, the series converges on a disc of radius ρ slightly larger than 1, over K = Frac(W). The resulting ring is W†{t}, the union over ρ > 1 of the rings of series convergent on the disc of radius ρ; the same holds for W†{t_1,…,t_n}. 'W-M algebras' (weakly complete finitely generated algebras) are the quotients of these rings by ideals. He hesitates over whether to require the ideals to be closed and asks whether they are automatically closed.

The point: overconvergent series are stable under termwise integration up to a constant. If |a_n| ≤ Cρ^{-n}, then |a_n|/|n+1| ≤ C(n+1)ρ^{-n}, which is O(ρ'^{-n}) for any 1 < ρ' < ρ. So on W†{t}, d: f ↦ f' has image all of W†{t} up to torsion, and H^1 of the affine line becomes 0 after ⊗Q. This is the motivation for Monsky–Washnitzer cohomology. The next page states the lifting theorem: smooth affine k-algebras lift to flat W-M algebras, uniquely up to non-unique isomorphism. It also states the functoriality of de Rham cohomology of dagger algebras.
errors: The displayed condition |a_n| = O(1) ρ^n with ρ > 1 is a slip as written: it allows growing coefficients. Convergence on a disc of radius ρ > 1 means |a_n| = O(ρ^{-n}), i.e. O(r^n) with r < 1. The surrounding text ('séries convergentes sur un disque de rayon ρ > 1') makes the intended meaning clear.
Minor: 'K̄ corps des fractions de K' should presumably read 'K corps des fractions de W'.

ideas.what: Replacing restricted (Tate) power series by overconvergent series to make p-adic de Rham cohomology of smooth affine varieties well behaved (integration preserves the ring up to torsion).
ideas.modern_name: Monsky–Washnitzer dagger algebras W†{t_1..t_n}, weak completion
ideas.where_published: Possibly mentioned in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); unsure

ideas.what: Question whether ideals of W†{t_1..t_n} are automatically closed, i.e. whether quotients by arbitrary ideals behave well.
ideas.modern_name: Noetherianity of dagger algebras / closedness of ideals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fulton (1969, Noetherianity of weakly complete algebras); Monsky–Washnitzer

deep.surprise_reason: This is a faithful expository summary of the Monsky–Washnitzer overconvergence idea, with a sign slip in the exponent. Grothendieck's motivation via the infinite-rank H^1 of the Tate algebra is the standard one. Nothing here goes beyond the literature.
transcription_corrections: Superscript insertion likely reads 'de divisibilité des coefficients' rather than 'de divisions de conditions'.
'(K̄ corps des fractions de K)' → probably '(K corps des fractions de W)'.
'un pas plus grand' → 'un peu plus grand'.
The displayed formula in the image is '|a_n| = O(1) ρ^n' (sic); the mathematically intended form is ρ^{-n}.
The ending '(les idéaux sont-ils' continues on the next page as 'automatiquement fermés)', not 'anto[?]contiguement[?] finis'.
